title: From RLVR to RLSVR: Task Transformation Induces Self-Verifiable Rewards for Open-Ended LLM Self-Improvement
data_curation: No human labels, reward models or judges are used in training. Only cheap document-level inputs are needed: GovReport long government reports (summarization), WritingPrompts (creative writing), and Nemotron-CC-Math-v1 source text (math, where players must design and solve a problem from the material). A follow-up run trains on PubMed. Supervision comes from an information-degradation operator g(.): the one spy among n players gets the input with a continuous span masked (20% for summarization and writing, 40% for math, since math text is more redundant). Civilians get the full input. The spy index is sampled uniformly, so the detection reward I[vote = spy] is verifiable by construction. Masking at 20% vs 40% gives nearly identical summarization results.
curriculum: Not a staged pipeline; training is RL self-play from Qwen3 models (the appendix names Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as the actor) for 100 iterations. The key schedule is alternation between a Performing stage and a Detection stage, with only one updated at a time. A hysteresis gate decides the switch: go from Detection to Performing when EMA detection accuracy is at least 0.9 and the N/A rate at most 0.1; go back when the error rate is at least 0.4 or the N/A rate at least 0.5; each phase lasts at least 5 updates. Joint simultaneous updating instead degrades math (5-benchmark average 42.4 to 35.3), while alternating raises it to 50.8.
method: RLSVR (RL with Self-Verifiable Rewards) is a paradigm that transforms an unverifiable task into a proxy environment. The environment injects a latent variable z, the policy performs the original task on observations built from (x, z), the outputs must answer a question about z, and a rule-based reward checks that answer against z, playing the role of a pretext task in self-supervised learning. The SpyRL instantiation is a 'Who Is the Spy?' game: n=5 players (n-1 civilians with full input, 1 spy with degraded input) do the same task, then each votes for the spy. Detection reward is 1 for a correct vote, with GRPO-style group normalization. Performer reward is zero-sum and vote-based: r_spy = -beta(m_u - mean m_c); each civilian gets beta/|C| (m_u - mean m_c) - lambda(m_j - mean m_c). Role-Advantage Estimation subtracts per-role EMA baselines; without it the 7-benchmark average drops to 37.5 from 50.4. Both stages use GRPO clipped objectives with low-variance KL 0.001, LR 1e-6, 128 prompts x 8 rollouts (effective batch 1024), max response 4,096, verl on 8 GPUs with vLLM TP=8.
eval_metrics: Summarization: ROUGE-L on GovReport, Multi-News, QMSum, VCSum, SAMSum (plus arXiv, PubMed, BillSum), with GPT-4o pairwise A/B win rates using swapped-order conservative aggregation. Creative writing: GPT-4o A/B on WritingPrompts and WritingBench across novelty, emotion, coherence, consistency and overall. Also a blinded human study (10 PhD students, 400 prompts), Gemini-3.5-Flash as an alternative judge, and GPT-4o-vs-human agreement (overall precision 91.0%, recall 93.8%). Reasoning: accuracy on GSM8K, MATH500, AIME24/25, Minerva, MMLU-Pro, GPQA-Diamond, plus AMC, OlympiadBench and SuperGPQA. Headline: Qwen3-4B GovReport ROUGE-L 36.7 vs 33.2 for Absolute Zero. Win rates versus own base: 73.9% / 75.4% summarization average and 81.3% / 76.5% WritingPrompts overall for 4B / 8B. Qwen3-4B reasoning: GSM8K 93.4, MATH500 79.5, AIME25 20.0, GPQA-D 41.3 (base 84.5 / 68.2 / 6.7 / 26.3).
key_results: SpyRL beats the R-Zero and Absolute Zero self-play baselines on every summarization and creative-writing benchmark (R-Zero even degrades creative writing to 48.8% vs base), and improves Qwen3-4B/8B math reasoning across seven benchmarks (4B average 41.4 to 50.4). Without any external verifier it beats a Qwen3.5-27B rubric-as-reward baseline (59.3% overall win on WritingPrompts) and is roughly on par with GPT-4o-RaR (48.9%), which cost about $900 in verifier calls.
evolution_note: RLSVR takes the verifiable-reward machinery behind o1/DeepSeek-R1-style RLVR (GRPO) and the label-by-construction idea of self-supervised pretext tasks (masked LM, contrastive learning). It aims them at open-ended generation, which until now relied on RLHF/DPO, LLM-as-judge, self-rewarding or rubric-as-reward signals that bring judge bias and cost. It extends proposer-solver self-play (Absolute Zero, R-Zero), which needs verifiable solver feedback, to multi-agent information-asymmetric games, and borrows Role-Advantage Estimation from prior multi-agent self-play RL. The broader claim is that verifiability can be engineered rather than being a fixed property of a task.
